title: Arizona Gifted & Talented
description: Cognitive abilities prep - verbal, quantitative, and spatial reasoning puzzles

questions.question: Bird is to nest as bee is to:
questions.explanation: A bird lives in a nest; a bee lives in a hive. This is a functional analogy (animal to its home).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: look for the hidden pattern - the lizard always finds the missing scale!

questions.question: Which word does NOT belong: Apple, Banana, Carrot, Grape?
questions.explanation: Apple, banana, and grape are fruits; a carrot is a vegetable. It is the odd one out by category.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy sniffs each word like a dinosaur detective - one of these is not like the others!

questions.question: Book is to library as car is to:
questions.explanation: A book is stored in a library; a car is stored in a garage. This is a thing-to-its-storage-place analogy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy parked her tiny car in the garage and roared: things belong where they belong!

questions.question: Happy is to joyful as sad is to:
questions.explanation: Happy and joyful are synonyms; sad and gloomy are synonyms. Match the pair with the same relationship.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy grins: happy and joyful are dino-buddies, so find the buddy of sad!

questions.question: Petal is to flower as brick is to:
questions.explanation: A petal is one part of a flower; a brick is one part of a wall. This is a part-to-whole analogy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy stacks bricks with her tail: small parts build big things - spot the whole!

questions.question: Rain is to flood as spark is to:
questions.explanation: Heavy rain can cause a flood; a spark can cause a fire. This is a cause-to-effect analogy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy watches a tiny spark grow: little causes make big effects - roar if you see it too!

questions.question: Which word does NOT belong: Whale, Seal, Dolphin, Eagle?
questions.explanation: Whale, seal, and dolphin are all mammals that live in the ocean; the eagle is a bird that flies in the sky. The eagle is the odd one out.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy splashes with her ocean friends, then spots one soaring overhead - who does not belong?

questions.question: Hot is to cold as day is to:
questions.explanation: Hot and cold are opposites; day and night are opposites. Match the pair with the same antonym relationship.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy flips the coin: hot-cold, day-night - opposites attract in this dino game!

questions.question: Which word does NOT belong: Hammer, Saw, Wrench, Ladder?
questions.explanation: Hammer, saw, and wrench are hand tools you hold; a ladder is climbing equipment, not a hand tool. It is the odd one out by category.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy opens her toolbox with tiny claws: three of these fit in her paws - one does not!

questions.question: Puppy is to dog as kitten is to:
questions.explanation: A puppy is a baby dog; a kitten is a baby cat. This is a young-to-adult analogy - match the right adult animal.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy cuddles the baby dinos: every little one grows into a big one - find the grown-up!

questions.question: The young ___ practiced its roar in the canyon.
questions.explanation: Only a lion roars; the canyon setting fits a land animal.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: read the whole sentence - the clues are hiding in plain sight!

questions.question: Which word does NOT belong: hammer, saw, wrench, apple?
questions.explanation: Hammer, saw, and wrench are tools; an apple is a fruit.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy stomps out the odd one - tools in the toolbox, fruit in the lunchbox!

questions.question: The ___ soared above the clouds, its wings spread wide.
questions.explanation: Only an eagle soars above clouds; penguins, turtles, and ants cannot fly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy flaps his tiny arms and wishes he could soar like that too!

questions.question: Which word does NOT belong: river, lake, ocean, desert?
questions.explanation: River, lake, and ocean are bodies of water; a desert is dry land.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy splashes in the water words and stays dusty-dry away from the desert one!

questions.question: Although the storm was fierce, the sailors remained ___ throughout the night.
questions.explanation: The word 'although' signals contrast with 'fierce storm', so the sailors stayed calm.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: watch for sneaky contrast words like 'although' - they flip the meaning!

questions.question: Which word does NOT belong: piano, violin, trumpet, bicycle?
questions.explanation: Piano, violin, and trumpet are musical instruments; a bicycle is a vehicle.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy bangs the piano keys but the bicycle just goes ring-ring instead of a tune!

questions.question: The chef added a ___ of salt to the soup to make it just right.
questions.explanation: A pinch is a small amount of salt for seasoning; a bucket, gallon, or pound would ruin the soup.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy sprinkles with his claws - just a pinch, not a whole bucket, please!

questions.question: Which word does NOT belong: ancient, antique, modern, old?
questions.explanation: Ancient, antique, and old all mean from long ago; modern means new or current.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy is ancient himself, so he spots the one word that is brand-new and shiny!

questions.question: The detective found a single ___ on the windowsill that cracked the whole case.
questions.explanation: A fingerprint is a clue a detective would use; a sandwich, blanket, or umbrella would not crack a case.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy dusts for clues with his tail - one tiny print can roar louder than a dinosaur!

questions.question: Which word does NOT belong: whisper, murmur, shout, mumble?
questions.explanation: Whisper, murmur, and mumble are all quiet speech; a shout is loud.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy whispers so he does not scare the fossils, but the odd word ROARS right out!

questions.question: Sun is to day as moon is to:
questions.explanation: The sun is the light of the day; the moon is the light of the night. This is a thing-to-its-time analogy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the sun clocks in for the day shift, the moon takes the night shift!

questions.question: Spider is to web as bird is to:
questions.explanation: A spider builds a web to live in; a bird builds a nest to live in. This is an animal-to-its-home analogy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: every builder has a home - silk for the spider, twigs for the bird!

questions.question: The opposite of "generous" is:
questions.explanation: Generous means giving freely; selfish means keeping things for yourself.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: be big-hearted like a dino sharing snacks!

questions.question: Calf is to cow as lamb is to:
questions.explanation: A calf is a baby cow; a lamb is a baby sheep. This is a young-to-adult analogy - match the right adult animal.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: farm babies grow up too - find each one's grown-up!

questions.question: The trail grew STEEP near the top of the mountain. The word STEEP most nearly means:
questions.explanation: STEEP describes a sharp upward slope, so slanted is the closest meaning.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: context is your treasure map - read around the word!

questions.question: Hammer is to nail as pen is to:
questions.explanation: A hammer is used on a nail; a pen is used on paper.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: match the tool to its teammate, like a dino and its roar!

questions.question: Tadpole is to frog as caterpillar is to:
questions.explanation: A tadpole grows into a frog; a caterpillar grows into a butterfly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: wiggly babies become fluttery flyers - nature is magic!

questions.question: If the day before yesterday was Monday, what day is tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Monday was two days ago, so today is Wednesday and tomorrow is Thursday.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: walk the days on your fingers like dino footprints!

questions.question: Book is to chapter as song is to:
questions.explanation: A chapter is one section of a book; a verse is one section of a song.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: big things are made of little pieces - crack the pattern!

questions.question: All BLOOPS are RAZZIES. Some RAZZIES are ZAZZLES. What must be true?
questions.correctAnswer: It is possible but not certain that some BLOOPS are ZAZZLES
questions.explanation: The RAZZIES that are ZAZZLES might not include any BLOOPS, so nothing is certain.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'all' and 'some' are sneaky words - stomp them carefully!

questions.question: What comes next? 2, 4, 8, 16, ?
questions.explanation: Each number doubles: 2x2=4, 4x2=8, 8x2=16, 16x2=32.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: numbers love to dance in patterns - watch their steps!

questions.question: What comes next? 3, 6, 11, 18, ?
questions.explanation: The gaps grow by 2 each time: 3 to 6 is +3, to 11 is +5, to 18 is +7, so add +9 next: 18+9=27.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: peek at the gaps between the numbers - sneaky patterns hide there!

questions.question: What comes next? 50, 45, 40, 35, ?
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sometimes the pattern marches backward - keep your tiny dino eyes open!

questions.question: What comes next? 5, 11, 7, 13, 9, ?
questions.explanation: Two patterns take turns: the odd spots grow 5, 7, 9 and the even spots grow 11, 13, so the next even spot is 15.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two lines of numbers are playing leapfrog - track each one separately!

questions.question: What comes next? 2, 6, 5, 15, 14, ?
questions.explanation: Multiply by 3, then subtract 1, over and over: 2x3=6, 6-1=5, 5x3=15, 15-1=14, 14x3=42.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: it goes hop, hop, hop - big leap, tiny step back, big leap again!

questions.question: What comes next? 10, 11, 13, 16, 20, ?
questions.explanation: Add 1 more each step: +1 gives 11, +2 gives 13, +3 gives 16, +4 gives 20, +5 gives 25.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the jumps keep growing - count how much bigger each hop is!

questions.question: What comes next? 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ?
questions.explanation: Add the last two numbers to make the next: 1+2=3, 2+3=5, 3+5=8, 5+8=13, 8+13=21.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each number is built from its two buddies right before it - teamwork!

questions.question: What comes next? 81, 27, 9, 3, ?
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: shrinking is a pattern too - what is eating each number?

questions.question: What comes next? 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: these numbers are square dancers in disguise - spot the square hiding inside!

questions.question: What comes next? 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, ?
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: clone the number, then toss in one extra bone - that is the recipe!

questions.question: I am an odd number between 20 and 30. My digits add up to 9. What number am I?
questions.explanation: Odd numbers between 20 and 30: 21, 23, 25, 27, 29. Their digit sums are 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. Only 27 sums to 9 (2+7=9).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: tiny digits, giant mystery - stomp through them one by one!

questions.question: If 2 owls catch 2 fish in 2 hours, how many owls are needed to catch 6 fish in 6 hours?
questions.explanation: Each owl catches 1 fish every 2 hours, so each owl catches 3 fish in 6 hours. Two owls catch 6 fish in 6 hours. Doubling the fish and the time cancels out.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: don't let the numbers trick you - roar at the rate, not the total!

questions.question: Sara is twice as old as her brother. Three years ago she was three times as old as he was. How old is Sara now?
questions.explanation: Let the brother's age be b, so Sara is 2b. Three years ago: 2b - 3 = 3(b - 3), which gives b = 6. Sara is 2 x 6 = 12.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: time travel is tricky, little dino - march backward through the years!

questions.question: What number comes next in this pattern: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.explanation: The gaps between the numbers grow by 2 each time: 4, 6, 8, 10. The next gap is 12, so 30 + 12 = 42.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: spot the pattern and pounce like a hungry raptor!

questions.question: If you write out all the numbers from 1 to 100, how many times does the digit 7 appear?
questions.explanation: The digit 7 appears 10 times in the ones place (7, 17, ..., 97) and 10 times in the tens place (70 through 79). 10 + 10 = 20.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: count like you are hunting snacks - check every hiding spot twice!

questions.question: If 4 builders can build 4 doghouses in 4 days, how many days will it take 8 builders to build 8 doghouses?
questions.explanation: Each builder builds 1 doghouse in 4 days. Eight builders each build 1 doghouse in the same 4 days, making 8 doghouses total.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: more helpers does not always mean more time - chomp the logic!

questions.question: A two-digit number has a tens digit that is 3 more than its ones digit. The two digits add up to 11. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Let the ones digit be x, so the tens digit is x + 3. Their sum is 2x + 3 = 11, so x = 4. The number is 74.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two clues, two digits - sniff them out like dino tracks!

questions.question: I pick a number, add 5 to it, then double the result and get 24. What was my number?
questions.explanation: Work backward: half of 24 is 12, and 12 minus 5 is 7. Check: (7 + 5) x 2 = 24.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: run the machine backward, hero - reverse stomp for the win!

questions.question: A magic machine doubles a number and then subtracts 3. If 17 comes out, what number went in?
questions.explanation: Undo the steps in reverse: add back the 3 to get 20, then halve it to get 10. Check: 10 x 2 - 3 = 17.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: undo the spell step by step - even wizards double-check!

questions.question: Ben is 10 years older than Lily. In 5 years, Ben will be twice as old as Lily is right now. How old is Lily now?
questions.explanation: Let Lily's age be L, so Ben is L + 10. In 5 years Ben will be L + 15, which equals 2L. So L + 15 = 2L, giving L = 15.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ages are just numbers wearing party hats - do the dino math!

questions.question: If star = 4 and moon = 6, what is star + moon + star?
questions.explanation: star + moon + star = 4 + 6 + 4 = 14.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: crack the code - every symbol is a secret number!

questions.question: If triangle = 2 and circle = 5, what is triangle + triangle + circle?
questions.explanation: triangle + triangle + circle = 2 + 2 + 5 = 9.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy is counting on its claws: two triangles and a circle, add them up!

questions.question: On a balance scale, 2 squares weigh the same as 1 circle. How many circles weigh the same as 4 squares?
questions.explanation: 2 squares = 1 circle, so 4 squares = 2 circles.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy balances on its tiny arms to check: double the squares, double the circles!

questions.question: A machine turns 2 into 5, 3 into 7, and 4 into 9. What does the machine turn 5 into?
questions.explanation: The machine doubles the number and adds 1: 5 doubled is 10, plus 1 is 11.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy loves mystery machines: double it, add one, and roar the answer!

questions.question: If diamond = 10 and star = 4, what is diamond - star - star?
questions.explanation: diamond - star - star = 10 - 4 - 4 = 2.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy munches the symbols away one by one: 10, take 4, take 4 more!

questions.question: 3 ribbons are used to make 1 wreath. How many ribbons are needed to make 4 wreaths?
questions.explanation: Each wreath needs 3 ribbons, so 4 wreaths need 4 x 3 = 12 ribbons.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy is decorating the jungle: ribbons come in groups of three, keep on counting!

questions.question: A machine turns 1 into 4, 2 into 7, and 3 into 10. What does the machine turn 5 into?
questions.explanation: The machine triples the number and adds 1: 5 x 3 = 15, plus 1 is 16.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy cracked the secret pattern: triple, add one, and stomp with pride!

questions.question: If box + box = 12 and box + triangle = 9, what is triangle?
questions.explanation: box + box = 12 means box = 6. Then 6 + triangle = 9, so triangle = 3.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy solved the first clue first, then used it to unlock the second. Clever dino!

questions.question: If heart = 5, what is heart + heart + heart?
questions.explanation: heart + heart + heart = 5 + 5 + 5 = 15.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy's big heart loves triples: three fives make a mighty roar!

questions.question: On a balance scale, 1 apple weighs the same as 2 bananas. How many bananas weigh the same as 5 apples?
questions.explanation: Each apple equals 2 bananas, so 5 apples = 5 x 2 = 10 bananas.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy is trading fruit at the jungle market: one apple is worth two bananas!

questions.question: What comes next? 2, 5, 4, 8, 6, 11, 8, ?
questions.explanation: Two patterns run side by side. Odd positions: 2, 4, 6, 8 (add 2). Even positions: 5, 8, 11 (add 3), so 11+3=14.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two sneaky number snakes hiding in one trail - track them both!

questions.question: T-Rexy thinks of a number. She multiplies it by 4, adds 8, then divides by 5. The answer is 12. What was her number?
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: reverse the rampage - stomp backwards through every step!

questions.question: What comes next? 5, 11, 23, 47, ?
questions.explanation: Double it and add 1 each time: 5 x 2 + 1 = 11, 11 x 2 + 1 = 23, 23 x 2 + 1 = 47, 47 x 2 + 1 = 95.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: these numbers are doubling down like a volcano ready to ROAR!

questions.question: T-Rexy owns 3 party hats and 4 capes. How many different hat-and-cape outfits can she wear?
questions.explanation: Each of the 3 hats pairs with each of the 4 capes: 3 x 4 = 12 outfits.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: mix and match, chomp and stomp - every combo counts!

questions.question: A gem box costs $15. A magic key costs $4 less than twice the gem box. What is the total cost of one gem box and one key?
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: unlock the key price first, then the treasure total is yours!

questions.question: What comes next? 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ?
questions.explanation: These are square numbers: 1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 4x4, 5x5, so next is 6x6 = 36.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: perfect squares are the tidiest eggs in the dinosaur nest!

questions.question: A treasure chest opens with a 2-digit code. The digits add up to 12 and the first digit is twice the second digit. What is the code?
questions.explanation: Call the digits a and b: a = 2b and a + b = 12, so 3b = 12, b = 4, a = 8. Code: 84.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: crack the code and the gold is ALL yours, mighty detective!

questions.question: Find the missing number. 2 x 5 + 3 = 13, 4 x 3 + 5 = 17, 6 x 2 + 7 = ?
questions.explanation: Each line follows the same recipe: multiply the first two numbers, then add the third: 6 x 2 + 7 = 12 + 7 = 19.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: same recipe, new ingredients - follow the dino cookbook!

questions.question: What comes next? 90, 45, 50, 25, 30, ?
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: shrink it, grow it, shrink it - ride the number roller coaster!

questions.question: Five dinosaur friends stand in a line for ice cream. T-Rexy must stand first. How many different lines are possible?
questions.explanation: T-Rexy is fixed first, so arrange the other 4 in the remaining spots: 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 24.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: I called the front of the line - now shuffle my friends every which way!

questions.question: A pattern goes: circle, square, circle, square, ?. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The shapes alternate circle, square, so circle comes next.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: spot the rhythm - shapes love to march in line!

questions.question: Three shapes grow bigger each step: small triangle, medium triangle, ?. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The size grows one step each time: small, medium, large - and the shape stays a triangle.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: growing like a dino from baby to mighty - follow the size!

questions.question: An arrow spins: it points up, then right, then down, then left. Where does it point next?
questions.explanation: The arrow turns 90 degrees clockwise each step; after left it returns to up.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: round and round like a dino doing the twist!

questions.question: A pattern goes: red circle, red circle, blue square, red circle, red circle, ?. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The repeating block is red circle, red circle, blue square, so blue square comes next.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: find the tiny herd that keeps repeating - then catch its tail!

questions.question: Each step adds one dot: 1 dot, 2 dots, 3 dots, ?. How many dots come next?
questions.explanation: The count grows by one each step: 1, 2, 3, so 4 comes next.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: count the dino footprints - each step leaves one more!

questions.question: A pattern goes: red, blue, green, red, blue, ?. What color comes next?
questions.explanation: The three-color cycle red, blue, green repeats, so green follows blue.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: paint the cycle in your mind - colors parade one by one!

questions.question: A flag waves and flips each step: it points right, then left, then right, then left. It also shrinks each time. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The direction alternates right, left, and the size keeps shrinking, so next is an even smaller flag pointing right.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: watch TWO clues at once - direction dances while size sneaks down!

questions.question: A pattern doubles the squares each step: 1 square, 2 squares, 4 squares, ?. How many squares come next?
questions.explanation: The number of squares doubles each step: 1, 2, 4, so 8 comes next.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: doubling like dino eggs hatching - watch the herd explode!

questions.question: A pattern cycles shape and size together: small circle, big square, small circle, big square, ?. What comes next?
questions.explanation: Shape and size change together in a two-step cycle: small circle, big square repeat.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: shape and size hold hands - they switch together like dino buddies!

questions.question: Dots shrink and move: big dot on top, medium dot in the middle, ?. What comes next?
questions.explanation: Both size and position change one step at a time: shrinking size and moving downward.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: shrinking and sinking like a tiny dino sliding down a hill - whee!

questions.question: Which does NOT belong? circle, square, triangle, rectangle
questions.explanation: Square, triangle, and rectangle all have straight sides and corners; a circle has no straight sides and no corners.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: one of these is NOT like the others - stomp it out!

questions.question: Which of these has the MOST corners? triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon
questions.explanation: A hexagon has 6 corners, more than a pentagon (5), a square (4), or a triangle (3).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: count the corners like dino claws - who has the most?

questions.question: All of these have 4 sides except one. Which one? square, rectangle, triangle, diamond
questions.explanation: A triangle has only 3 sides; a square, a rectangle, and a diamond each have 4 sides.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: four shapes, three match - find the one that roars different!

questions.question: Which does NOT belong? square, cube, triangle, pentagon
questions.explanation: A cube is a 3D solid shape; a square, a triangle, and a pentagon are flat 2D shapes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: flat like a footprint or chunky like a fossil? Spot the odd one!

questions.question: Which does NOT belong? red circle, blue circle, green circle, red square
questions.explanation: The red, blue, and green figures are all circles; only the red square is a different shape.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: same shape club - but one snuck in wearing a disguise!

questions.question: Which shape does NOT have a line of symmetry? square, heart, scalene triangle, arrow
questions.explanation: A scalene triangle has no line of symmetry; a square, a heart, and an arrow each have at least one.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fold it in your mind - which one does not mirror back?

questions.question: Which of these has an ODD number of sides? hexagon, rectangle, octagon, pentagon
questions.explanation: A pentagon has 5 sides, an odd number; a hexagon has 6, a rectangle has 4, and an octagon has 8 - all even.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: odd numbers are sneaky - count the sides, little dino detective!

questions.question: Which solid has exactly ONE flat face? cylinder, cone, cube, pyramid
questions.explanation: A cone has exactly one flat face (its circular base) plus one curved surface; a cylinder has 2 flat faces, a cube has 6, and a square pyramid has 5.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: count the flat faces on these rocky shapes - one is special!

questions.question: Which does NOT belong? circle, ring, letter O, letter C
questions.explanation: A circle, a ring, and the letter O are closed loops; the letter C is open - it has two ends.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: follow the loop - which one has an escape route?

questions.question: Which of these CANNOT roll? cube, sphere, cylinder, cone
questions.explanation: A sphere, a cylinder, and a cone all have curved surfaces and can roll; a cube has only flat faces, so it cannot roll.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: give it a push - which shape refuses to roll?

questions.question: First: small circle. Second: big circle. Third: small square. What comes fourth?
questions.explanation: Size grows (small to big) and shape changes (circle to square); the fourth combines both: big square.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: follow the transformation trail - every change leaves footprints!

questions.question: An arrow points up, then right, then down. Which way does it point next?
questions.explanation: The arrow turns one quarter-turn clockwise each time: up to right to down, so next is left.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: spin, little arrow, spin! Tiny T-Rex arms can point the way too!

questions.question: A paper arrow points left. You hold it up to a mirror. Which way does the mirror arrow point?
questions.explanation: A mirror flips left and right, so a left-pointing arrow points right in the mirror.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: mirrors are like pond water - left becomes right with a big splash!

questions.question: Row 1: one dot, two dots, three dots. Row 2: one star, two stars, ?. What fills the blank?
questions.explanation: Row 2 follows the same counting pattern as Row 1 (1, 2, 3) but with stars, so the blank is three stars.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: rows are like dinosaur egg nests - fill every egg spot in the right order!

questions.question: Which shape does NOT belong: red circle, red square, blue triangle, red triangle?
questions.explanation: Every other shape is red; only the blue triangle breaks the color pattern.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: spot the dino that is not like the others - you are a true pattern hunter!

questions.question: A circle sits inside a triangle. Next, a triangle sits inside a square. Next, a square sits inside a pentagon. What comes next?
questions.explanation: Each step, the inner shape moves out to become the outer shape, and the new outer shape has one more side: the triangle (3 sides) holds the circle, the square (4 sides) holds the triangle, the pentagon (5 sides) holds the square, so next the hexagon (6 sides) holds the pentagon.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: shapes grow sides the way T-Rexy grows teeth - one more each time, chomp!

questions.question: A square is split into 4 corners. The dark corner moves: top-left, then top-right, then bottom-right. Where is it next?
questions.explanation: The dark corner marches clockwise around the square: top-left to top-right to bottom-right, so next is bottom-left.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the dark corner is playing hide-and-seek - stomp after it and you win!

questions.question: First: 1 star. Second: 2 stars. Third: 1 circle. What comes fourth?
questions.explanation: The count repeats 1-2-1-2 while the shape switches from star to circle; the fourth is 2 circles.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: one-two, one-two - stomp the counting rhythm and the answer roars out!

questions.question: A square is dark on its left half. It turns one quarter-turn clockwise three times. Where is the dark half now?
questions.explanation: Each turn moves the dark half one quarter clockwise: left to top (1), top to right (2), right to bottom (3).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: spin the fossil round and round - watch where the dark half stomps to!

questions.question: Row 1: circle with 1 line, circle with 2 lines, circle with 3 lines. Row 2: square with 1 line, square with 2 lines, ?. What fills the blank?
questions.explanation: Row 2 copies Row 1's growing line count (1, 2, 3) but on a square, so the blank is a square with 3 lines.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: every row tells a fossil story - finish the last page like a detective!
